full_judgment:
2. It appears that the plaintiffs including the petitioner brought OC Suit No. 199 of 1994 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar for declaration of title and partition. The defendant-appellant-respondent contested the suit by filing a written statement claiming, inter alia, title to and possession in part of the suit land. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit whereupon the said defendant-respondents filed First Appeal No. 393 of 1996 and thereafter filed an application for temporary injunction which was granted by the impugned order. Now this petition for leave to appeal from the same. 

 5. It appears to be somewhat unusual that an order of injunction has been passed against the decree-holder plaintiffs on the mere assertion of the defendants against whom the trial Court has found both inspect of title and possession and the said judgment is yet to be set aside. The defendant-appellants could have prayed for an order staying the operation of the impugned judgment and decree if there was any truth in their assertion that being emboldened by the decree the plaintiffs were taking steps to dispossess the defendants. The defendant-appellants could pray for a stay of further proceedings if the decree was put into execution but instead of following such usual course they made the unusual prayer for injunction in a case like this and also succeeded.
